claims.text: The target materials are eutectic high-entropy alloys containing dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Introducing coherent nanoprecipitations can improve strength in eutectic high-entropy alloys relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Introducing coherent nanoprecipitations can improve room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Coherent nanoprecipitation interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitations relieve stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
Facilitated dislocation transmission and relieved stress concentrations are the mechanisms by which coherent nanoprecipitations improve both strength and tensile ductility.
The proposed benefit is limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys having a specific composition and microstructure.
The exact composition and processing conditions needed to produce the desired response are uncertain.
A controlled tensile comparison of alloys with and without coherent nanoprecipitations can test the hypothesis.
Failure of the nanoprecipitation-treated material to improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
